name: Nguyen Hue Walking Street
summary: Walking street from City Hall to Bạch Đằng: stroll the paving at sundown, the liveliest hour on this block. Towers, restaurants, and shops line both sides. City Hall at 86 Lê Thánh Tôn stays closed to the public. Apartment 42 is a former residential block of cafes and shops along the walk.
timeNeeded: A walk, longer if you go into Apartment 42. Check on arrival.
fee: Check on arrival. No fee for the street was printed.
getThere: This is the center if your room is on the square.
heroCaption: Nguyễn Huệ after dark: the paving, the crowd, and the buildings on both sides

notice.title: Bùi Viện is the night street
notice.body: Bùi Viện was branded the city’s second official walking street in 2017. It crosses Phạm Ngũ Lão. This paving is the sundown walk from City Hall to the river.

body: The walking street runs from City Hall to Bạch Đằng wharf. City Hall, the administrative seat of the People’s Committee, stands at 86 Lê Thánh Tôn and is closed to the public. You look at the front from the paving. The April 2025 proposal also places the political center at 86 Lê Thánh Tôn, Quận 1.

The night photograph is the paving with people between the buildings. The daylight frame is the same street earlier, with the towers on both sides. Apartment 42 Nguyễn Huệ is a former residential block of cafes and shops. The street itself is the walk.

figures.caption: The same paving in daylight, with the buildings on both sides
figures.alt: Nguyen Hue walking street in daylight, paving and towers

gettingThere: If you are staying on Đồng Khởi, you are already here. Hours of any closure to cars were not on the attractions page. Check on arrival.

hours: Vietnam Tourism says the street is liveliest at sundown. A pedestrian-only clock was not printed. Check on arrival.
